**Q: What is on the ProAdvisor exam?**
A: The QBO Certification covers setup and subscriptions, navigation and settings, list management, the chart of accounts, customer and sales workflows, vendor and purchase workflows, banking and reconciliation, reports, and payroll basics, roughly 50 questions per module, with an 80% passing score and 3 attempts per module.

**Q: How long does the ProAdvisor exam take?**
A: There is no strict time limit on most modules, but plan for several hours total since the certification is split across multiple modules with their own quizzes plus a final exam.

**Q: Do you need to be an accountant?**
A: No. Anyone can create a free QuickBooks Online Accountant account and complete the ProAdvisor certification, though it is designed for bookkeepers, accountants, and QuickBooks consultants.

**Q: How long is ProAdvisor certification valid?**
A: ProAdvisor certifications require annual recertification. Intuit notifies you when your certification exam needs to be retaken to stay current.

## Basic Life Support (BLS) (BLS)
Vendor: American Heart Association
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/bls/
Total questions: 300

BLS (Basic Life Support) certifies healthcare professionals to deliver high-quality CPR, use an AED, provide ventilation with barrier devices and bag-mask, relieve choking, and work as part of a high-performance resuscitation team for adults, children, and infants. Required for nurses, physicians, EMTs, paramedics, dental and respiratory professionals, and most clinical roles. Built around the AHA Chain of Survival, 2020 BLS Guidelines (with 2023 focused updates), and the AHA BLS Provider course; renewal is typically every two years.

### Domains
- 1.0 Course Concepts and Chain of Survival (6% of exam): 18 questions
- 2.0 Assessment and High-Performance Teams (12% of exam): 36 questions
- 3.0 Adult BLS (1- and 2-Rescuer) (22% of exam): 66 questions
- 4.0 Pediatric BLS (Children and Infants) (18% of exam): 54 questions
- 5.0 AED for All Ages (16% of exam): 48 questions
- 6.0 Alternate Ventilation and Advanced Airways (8% of exam): 24 questions
- 7.0 Choking Relief Across Ages (10% of exam): 30 questions
- 8.0 Special Emergencies and Recovery (8% of exam): 24 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: What is on the AHA BLS exam?**
A: The BLS written exam covers the Chain of Survival, high-quality CPR for adults, children, and infants, AED use, ventilation with a bag-mask device, choking relief, and working as part of a resuscitation team. It pairs with a hands-on skills test for the in-person provider card.

**Q: What is BLS Exam A vs Exam B?**
A: The AHA issues two equivalent 25-question versions, Exam A and Exam B, so instructors can give a different version on a retake. Both cover the same content at the same difficulty; QuizBuffet’s question bank draws from both.

**Q: What is the passing score for BLS?**
A: You need 84%, or 21 of 25 questions correct, on the written exam, plus a successful hands-on skills check.

**Q: Is the BLS test online?**
A: The knowledge portion can be completed online through AHA HeartCode BLS, but you still need an in-person skills session with an instructor to get the provider card. QuizBuffet’s free practice test and mock test questions cover that online knowledge portion.

**Q: How long is BLS valid?**
A: BLS certification from the American Heart Association is valid for two years, after which you renew with a shorter refresher course.

**Q: Is BLS the same as CPR?**
A: BLS builds on CPR and AED skills with additional content aimed at healthcare professionals: team-based resuscitation, advanced airway ventilation, and recognizing deterioration before cardiac arrest. A general CPR/AED course is aimed at lay rescuers and covers less ground.

## Cosmetology License (Cosmetology)
Vendor: State Boards
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/cosmetology-license/
Total questions: 300

A Cosmetology License is required in every U.S. state to perform haircutting, chemical services, skin care, and nail care for compensation. State exams typically follow the NIC (National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology) National Theory blueprint, administered by PSI or a similar testing vendor as a written exam plus a hands-on practical. The written exam covers four areas: scientific concepts (infection control, anatomy and physiology, chemistry, electricity), hair care and services (cutting, styling, color, chemical texture, hair structure), skin care and services (facials, hair removal, skin analysis), and nail care and services (manicures, pedicures, enhancements, nail disorders).

### Domains
- 1.0 Scientific Concepts (31% of exam): 92 questions
- 2.0 Hair Care and Services (37% of exam): 118 questions
- 3.0 Skin Care and Services (17% of exam): 49 questions
- 4.0 Nail Care and Services (15% of exam): 41 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: What is on the cosmetology state board written exam?**
A: Most states use the NIC National Cosmetology Theory exam or a state version of it. It covers scientific concepts (infection control, anatomy, chemistry), hair care and services, skin care and services, and nail care and services. A separate hands-on practical exam is also required in most states.

**Q: How many questions are on the cosmetology theory exam?**
A: Typically 90 to 110 multiple-choice questions with 90 minutes to two hours, depending on your state. Ten or so items are usually unscored pilot questions.

**Q: What is the passing score for the cosmetology exam?**
A: Your state board sets it. Most states require 70 to 75 percent on the written exam, and the practical is scored separately.

**Q: Can I take the cosmetology exam online?**
A: The written exam is usually taken at a PSI or Prometric testing center, and some states offer remote proctoring. The practical must be done in person on a mannequin or model.

**Q: How many hours do I need before I can sit for the cosmetology exam?**
A: It varies by state, most commonly 1,000 to 1,600 hours of approved school training. Check your state board because apprenticeship paths and reciprocity rules differ.

**Q: What happens if I fail the cosmetology exam?**
A: You can retake it after paying the exam fee again. Most states let you retake only the section you failed and have no long waiting period, but a few limit attempts before requiring more training.

## Advanced Practice Micropigmentation (Micropigmentation)
Vendor: NIC
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/micropigmentation/
Total questions: 210

The NIC National Advanced Practice Micropigmentation Theory Examination is the licensure theory exam for advanced cosmetic tattoo procedures (permanent makeup, paramedical micropigmentation, scalp pigmentation, areola restoration, scar repigmentation) authored by the National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology (NIC) and adopted by participating state boards. The blueprint covers three domains: Scientific Concepts (infection control, skin and tissue structure, human anatomy and physiology, skin disorders, equipment and pigment storage), Micropigmentation Procedures (client communication and documentation, skin preparation, color theory, pre-application design, and application technique), and Side Effects and Possible Complications. Candidates are expected to anchor their knowledge in the Society of Permanent Cosmetic Professionals (SPCP) standards, NIC Infection Control and Safety Standards, and Milady's Aesthetician Series Permanent Makeup: Tips and Techniques.

### Domains
- 1.0 Scientific Concepts (46% of exam): 96 questions
- 2.0 Micropigmentation Procedures (50% of exam): 104 questions
- 3.0 Side Effects and Possible Complications (4% of exam): 10 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: Bacteria that require oxygen to survive are classified as**
A: aerobic

**Q: The virus of greatest bloodborne transmission concern during micropigmentation procedures is**
A: hepatitis B

**Q: A client history record for micropigmentation must include**
A: current medications, allergies, medical conditions, previous cosmetic procedures, and skin conditions

**Q: Informed consent for a micropigmentation procedure must be obtained**
A: in writing before the procedure begins, after the technician has explained the procedure, risks, expected outcomes, and alternatives

**Q: The most common expected side effect immediately following a micropigmentation procedure is**
A: redness, mild swelling, and tenderness at the procedure site lasting 24-72 hours

**Q: A client who had brow micropigmentation performed two years ago is scheduled for an MRI of the head and neck. The most important safety step is**
A: inform the MRI technologist and radiologist about the presence of iron oxide-based micropigmentation pigments at the brow site so the imaging team can assess artifact risk, any potential local heating, and any sensation reported by the client during the scan

## Barber License (Barber)
Vendor: State Boards
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/barber-license/
Total questions: 260

A Barber License is required in every U.S. state to perform haircutting, shaving, beard design, chemical hair services, and basic skin and scalp care for compensation. Most states use the NIC (National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology) National Barber Theory Examination, a 60-item, 90-minute written exam, paired with a hands-on practical, both typically administered by PSI. The theory blueprint covers four domains: scientific concepts (infection control, anatomy and physiology, skin and hair disorders, product chemistry), implements and equipment (razors, shears, clippers, sanitation), hair care services (consultation, draping, shampoo, cutting, styling, chemical services), and facial hair and skin care services (shaving, facial hair design, facials, electrotherapy).

### Domains
- 1.0 Scientific Concepts (38% of exam): 100 questions
- 2.0 Implements and Equipment (8% of exam): 20 questions
- 3.0 Hair Care Services (40% of exam): 104 questions
- 4.0 Facial Hair and Skin Care Services (14% of exam): 36 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: What is on the barber state board written exam?**
A: Most states use the NIC National Barber Theory exam or a state version of it. It covers scientific concepts (infection control, anatomy, chemistry), hair care services, facial hair and skin care services, and implements and equipment. A hands-on practical exam is also required in most states.

**Q: How many questions are on the barber theory exam?**
A: The NIC barber theory exam has 60 items, of which 50 are scored, with 90 minutes to complete it. State versions vary slightly.

**Q: What is the passing score for the barber exam?**
A: Your state board sets it. Most states require 70 to 75 percent on the written exam, and the practical is scored separately.

**Q: How many training hours do I need for a barber license?**
A: It varies by state, most commonly 1,000 to 1,500 hours of barber school or an approved apprenticeship. Check your state board for its exact requirement and any reciprocity rules.

**Q: Can I take the barber exam online?**
A: The written exam is usually taken at a PSI or Prometric testing center, and some states offer remote proctoring. The practical must be done in person on a live model or mannequin.

**Q: What happens if I fail the barber exam?**
A: You can retake it after paying the exam fee again. Most states let you retake only the section you failed with no long waiting period, but some limit attempts before requiring more training.

## Barber 1 (No Chemical) License (Barber 1)
Vendor: State Boards
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/barber-no-chemical/
Total questions: 220

Barber 1 (No Chemical) is an entry-level barber license that authorizes haircutting, shaving, beard and facial-hair design, and basic styling, but NOT chemical services such as color, perms, or relaxers. It requires fewer training hours than a full Barber License and is a common stepping stone toward chemical-services certification. Most states use the NIC (National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology) National Barber 1 (No Chemical) Theory Examination, a 60-item (50 weighted), 90-minute written exam. The blueprint covers four domains: scientific concepts (infection control, anatomy and physiology, skin and hair disorders, basic product chemistry, 40%), implements and equipment (razors, shears, clippers, sanitation, 10%), hair care services (consultation, draping, shampoo, cutting, styling, 30%), and facial hair and skin care services (shaving, facial hair design, facials, electrotherapy, 20%).

### Domains
- 1.0 Scientific Concepts (40% of exam): 88 questions
- 2.0 Implements and Equipment (11% of exam): 24 questions
- 3.0 Hair Care Services (31% of exam): 68 questions
- 4.0 Facial Hair and Skin Care Services (18% of exam): 40 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: Direct contact transmission of pathogens occurs primarily through which of the following?**
A: Physical touch with an infected person or their blood and body fluids

**Q: Which bacterial shape classification is known for producing resistant spores that can survive standard disinfection procedures?**
A: Bacilli

**Q: Which of the following is considered a major piece of equipment in a barbershop rather than an implement or supply?**
A: The barber chair, which supports and positions the client during services

**Q: A hydraulic barber chair is considered essential equipment primarily because it accomplishes which of the following?**
A: It allows the barber to adjust the client's height and position for ergonomic and effective service delivery

**Q: Scalp analysis is performed before a service primarily to accomplish which of the following?**
A: To identify scalp and hair conditions that may affect service selection and product choices

**Q: A contraindication in barbering is BEST defined as which of the following?**
A: A condition or circumstance that prohibits a service or requires significant service modification

## Tattoo Artist License (Tattoo)
Vendor: NIC
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/tattoo-license/
Total questions: 88

A Tattoo Artist License is required in most U.S. states to perform tattooing for compensation. Many states use the NIC (National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology) National Tattooing Practical Examination, a six-section, timed performance evaluation administered on a live model. The exam covers six core domains based on the national job analysis: Work Area Set Up (infection control, EPA-registered disinfection, OSHA-mandated disposal containers, supply preparation), Client Preparation and Stencil Application (skin prep, simulated shave, stencil transfer to the forearm), Machine Assembly (presenting sterile packaged tubes and needles, building the machine, power on/off testing), Demonstration of Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion (pigment dispersal, simulated application, mid-procedure ink-cap addition, conclusion), Breakdown and Conclusion of Tattoo Service (decontaminating the procedural area, completing personal protection procedures), and Work Area Set Up for New Client (re-preparing supplies, demonstrating foot-switch disinfection and transport, completing personal protection). References are anchored on Milady Standard Esthetics Fundamentals + Foundations (12th Edition) and the APP Procedure Manual.

### Domains
- 1.0 Work Area Set Up (18% of exam): 16 questions
- 2.0 Client Preparation and Stencil Application (14% of exam): 12 questions
- 3.0 Machine Assembly (14% of exam): 12 questions
- 4.0 Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion (23% of exam): 20 questions
- 5.0 Breakdown and Conclusion of Tattoo Service (18% of exam): 16 questions
- 6.0 Work Area Set Up for New Client (13% of exam): 12 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: Before beginning any tattoo procedure, the artist must don which personal protective equipment at minimum?**
A: Medical-grade disposable gloves

**Q: During the NIC Tattooing Practical Examination, the razor used for the simulated shave must be**
A: capped throughout the simulated shaving demonstration

**Q: Before beginning machine assembly, the candidate must present the packaged tube and needle to the examiner to**
A: demonstrate that the tube and needle are sterile by showing intact, uncompromised original packaging before opening

**Q: Pigment must be dispensed from the source bottle into a**
A: single-use ink cap placed on the procedure tray, never directly into the tube or machine

**Q: When breaking down the procedural work area after a tattoo service, barriers must be**
A: removed carefully to avoid touching the contaminated outer surface, then discarded in the 'Trash' container before the underlying surface is disinfected

**Q: When setting up supplies for a new client after breakdown, the candidate should**
A: begin with freshly disinfected or newly barriered surfaces and new sterile packaged implements from the supply kit, never reusing single-session items from the previous client's procedure

## CPA Auditing and Attestation (AUD) (AUD)
Vendor: AICPA
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/cpa-aud/
Total questions: 286

The Auditing and Attestation (AUD) section is one of three Core sections of the Uniform CPA Examination administered by the AICPA. Every CPA candidate must pass AUD regardless of their chosen Discipline. The 4-hour exam consists of 78 multiple-choice questions and 7 task-based simulations, weighted 50/50 in scoring. Content covers four areas: Ethics, Professional Responsibilities and General Principles (15-25%), AICPA Code of Conduct, SEC/PCAOB/GAO/DOL independence, professional skepticism, engagement preconditions, documentation; Assessing Risk and Developing a Planned Response (25-35%), engagement strategy, the COSO Internal Control. Integrated Framework, IT general controls, SOC 1® reports, materiality and tolerable misstatement, fraud risk, related parties, single audits; Performing Further Procedures and Obtaining Evidence (30-40%), sampling, tests of controls and details, analytical procedures, external confirmations, audit data analytics, accounting estimates, going concern, subsequent events; and Forming Conclusions and Reporting (10-20%): audit and attestation reports, opinion types, emphasis-of-matter paragraphs, compilation and review engagements, compliance reporting, special-purpose frameworks, and additional GAO reporting requirements. References include AICPA Statements on Auditing Standards, PCAOB Auditing Standards, GAO Government Auditing Standards, Single Audit Act, OMB 2 CFR 200, and the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct.

### Domains
- 1.0 Ethics, Professional Responsibilities and General Principles (20% of exam): 56 questions
- 2.0 Assessing Risk and Developing a Planned Response (30% of exam): 86 questions
- 3.0 Performing Further Procedures and Obtaining Evidence (28% of exam): 80 questions
- 4.0 Forming Conclusions and Reporting (22% of exam): 64 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: IRC §6694(b) imposes a penalty on a tax return preparer for willful or reckless conduct. What conduct triggers this penalty, and what is the penalty amount?**
A: Willful attempt to understate tax liability; reckless or intentional disregard of rules or regulations; penalty = the greater of $5,000 or 75% of the income derived from the return

**Q: Under IRC §6695, which of the following is a penalty imposed on a tax return preparer?**
A: Failure to include the preparer's Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN) on the return, $50 per failure, up to a maximum of $27,000 per year

**Q: Establishing an overall audit strategy at the beginning of an engagement serves to**
A: Set the scope, timing, and direction of the audit and guide the development of the more detailed engagement plan

**Q: Which of the following decisions is BEST characterized as part of the overall audit strategy rather than the more detailed engagement plan?**
A: The determination that the audit will rely primarily on substantive analytical procedures rather than tests of controls in areas where the assessed control environment is weak

**Q: In performing audit procedures, auditors commonly use data from which two primary sources?**
A: Entity-produced data (accounting records, transaction files, master files) and external data (market prices, third-party records, industry benchmarks)

**Q: Before using an entity-provided transaction data file to perform audit sampling, an auditor should verify the completeness and accuracy of the file. Which procedure is MOST appropriate for this purpose?**
A: Reconcile the file's record counts and total dollar amounts to independently prepared control totals, such as summary reports from the entity's accounting system or the trial balance

## CPA Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR) (FAR)
Vendor: AICPA
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/cpa-far/
Total questions: 280

The Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR) section is one of three Core sections of the Uniform CPA Examination administered by the AICPA. Every CPA candidate must pass FAR regardless of chosen Discipline. The 4-hour exam consists of 50 multiple-choice questions and 7 task-based simulations, weighted 50/50 in scoring. Content covers three areas: Financial Reporting (30-40%): preparation, adjustment, and analysis of financial statements for for-profit business entities and nongovernmental not-for-profit entities under the FASB Accounting Standards Codification, public company reporting under SEC rules (Forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K, EPS), special-purpose frameworks, financial statement ratios, and state and local government measurement focus and basis of accounting under GASB; Select Balance Sheet Accounts (30-40%): cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables, inventory, property plant and equipment, investments (fair value, amortized cost, equity method), intangible assets, payables and accrued liabilities, debt covenants, and equity transactions; and Select Transactions (25-35%): accounting changes and error corrections, contingencies and commitments, revenue recognition (five-step model and not-for-profit contributions), accounting for income taxes, fair value measurements, lessee accounting, and subsequent events. References include the FASB Accounting Standards Codification, FASB Concepts Statements, U.S. SEC Regulation S-X and S-K, GASB Codification, and AICPA Practice Aids.

### Domains
- 1.0 Financial Reporting (46% of exam): 128 questions
- 2.0 Select Balance Sheet Accounts (34% of exam): 96 questions
- 3.0 Select Transactions (20% of exam): 56 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: The fundamental accounting equation underlying the balance sheet states that**
A: Assets = Liabilities + Stockholders' Equity

**Q: Under US GAAP, an asset is classified as current on the balance sheet when**
A: It is expected to be converted to cash, sold, or consumed within one year or within the entity's operating cycle, whichever is longer

**Q: Under ASC 305, an investment qualifies as a cash equivalent when it is**
A: A short-term, highly liquid investment readily convertible to a known cash amount with an original maturity of three months or less from the date of purchase, presenting insignificant risk of value changes

**Q: On December 1, a company purchases a 60-day commercial paper instrument with face value of $500,000. How should this investment be classified on the December 31 balance sheet?**
A: Cash equivalent, the 60-day original maturity at purchase is within the three-month threshold, qualifying it as a cash equivalent

**Q: Under ASC 250, a change in accounting principle is generally accounted for using which approach?**
A: Retrospective approach, all prior periods presented are restated to reflect the new principle, and the cumulative effect on periods not presented is recorded as an adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings

**Q: A company changes depreciation method from declining balance to straight-line for all existing assets. This is classified as**
A: A change in accounting estimate effected by a change in accounting principle, accounted for prospectively in current and future periods

## CPA Taxation and Regulation (REG) (REG)
Vendor: AICPA
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/cpa-reg/
Total questions: 112

The Taxation and Regulation (REG) section is one of three Core sections of the Uniform CPA Examination administered by the AICPA. Every CPA candidate must pass REG regardless of chosen Discipline. The 4-hour exam consists of 72 multiple-choice questions and 8 task-based simulations, weighted 50/50 in scoring. Content covers five areas: Ethics, Professional Responsibilities and Federal Tax Procedures (10-20%). Treasury Department Circular 230, tax return preparer rules and penalties, state board licensing, IRS audits and appeals, tax authoritative hierarchy, privileged communications; Business Law (15-25%): agency, contracts (UCC), debtor-creditor relationships, bankruptcy under BAPCPA 2005, employment taxes, qualified health plans, worker classifications, anti-bribery under FCPA 1977, business entity formation and termination; Federal Taxation of Property Transactions (5-15%): tax basis of purchased and converted assets, gifted and inherited property, wash sales, intangible assets, MACRS depreciation, Section 179, amortization; Federal Taxation of Individuals (22-32%): Form 1040 gross income inclusions and exclusions, pass-through income, AGI adjustments, itemized deductions, QBI deduction, loss limitations, filing status, tax credits, estimated tax safe harbor; and Federal Taxation of Entities (23-33%): Schedule M-1/M-3 book-tax differences, C corporation taxable income and state nexus, S corporation eligibility and ordinary business income, partnership separately stated items and partner basis, LLCs, tax-exempt organizations. References include the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 as amended, Treasury Regulations, Uniform Commercial Code, Revised Model Business Corporation Act, FCPA, and ACA.

### Domains
- 1.0 Ethics, Professional Responsibilities and Federal Tax Procedures (14% of exam): 16 questions
- 2.0 Business Law (25% of exam): 28 questions
- 3.0 Federal Taxation of Property Transactions (14% of exam): 16 questions
- 4.0 Federal Taxation of Individuals (22% of exam): 24 questions
- 5.0 Federal Taxation of Entities (25% of exam): 28 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: Under Treasury Circular 230, which individuals are generally authorized to represent taxpayers before all levels of the Internal Revenue Service, including appeals and collections?**
A: Attorneys, certified public accountants (CPAs), and enrolled agents, all three hold unlimited practice rights before the IRS

**Q: In the hierarchy of federal tax authority, which source ranks HIGHEST and is therefore binding on both the IRS and taxpayers?**
A: The Internal Revenue Code (IRC), as enacted by Congress under its constitutional taxing authority, the IRC is the primary statutory source of federal tax law

**Q: Which type of agency authority arises when a third party reasonably believes an agent has authority because the principal's words or conduct created that impression, even though the agent has no actual authority?**
A: Apparent authority, authority that exists because the principal's conduct led the third party to reasonably believe the agent was authorized

**Q: Under common law contract principles, which of the following must be present for a valid contract to be formed?**
A: An offer, acceptance, consideration, contractual capacity, and legality of subject matter, all five elements must be present

**Q: A taxpayer inherits stock from a deceased relative who paid $10,000 for the stock. At the date of death, the stock's fair market value is $85,000. The taxpayer sells the stock for $90,000 nine months after inheriting it. What is the taxpayer's basis in the stock and the character of the gain?**
A: Basis = $85,000 (FMV at date of death, §1014 stepped-up basis); gain = $5,000 long-term capital gain (inherited property is always long-term)

**Q: A calendar-year taxpayer places a $50,000 piece of 5-year MACRS property into service on July 1. Assuming the half-year convention applies and the MACRS first-year rate for 5-year property is 20%, what is the first-year depreciation deduction?**
A: $10,000, the full 20% applies to the $50,000 cost because the asset was placed in service on July 1

## CPA Business Analysis and Reporting (BAR) (BAR)
Vendor: AICPA
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/cpa-bar/
Total questions: 100

The Business Analysis and Reporting (BAR) section is one of three Discipline sections of the Uniform CPA Examination administered by the AICPA. Candidates pass three Core sections (AUD, FAR, REG) plus one Discipline of their choice, BAR is most often selected by candidates planning a career in audit, advisory, financial reporting, or work with state and local governments. The 4-hour exam consists of 50 multiple-choice questions and 7 task-based simulations, weighted 50/50 in scoring. Content covers three areas: Business Analysis (40-50%): current-period financial statement analysis, non-financial and non-GAAP performance measures (balanced scorecard, EBITDA, customer retention, free cash flow), managerial and cost accounting, variance analysis, budgeting and forecasting, capital structure, cost of capital, investment valuation (NPV, IRR, payback), COSO Enterprise Risk Management framework and ESG-related risks, and the impact of economic and market influences on business; Technical Accounting and Reporting (35-45%): indefinite-lived intangible assets and goodwill, internally developed software, advanced revenue recognition, stock compensation, research and development costs, business combinations, consolidated financial statements (variable interest entities, noncontrolling interests, foreign currency translation), derivatives and hedge accounting, lessor accounting, SEC public company reporting (Regulation S-X, S-K, segments), and financial statements of employee benefit plans; and State and Local Governments (10-20%): government-wide, governmental fund, proprietary fund, and fiduciary fund financial statements under the GASB Codification, including capital assets, long-term liabilities, interfund activity, nonexchange revenue, and budgetary accounting. References include the FASB Accounting Standards Codification, GASB Statements, U.S. SEC Regulations, and the COSO ERM framework.

### Domains
- 1.0 Business Analysis (32% of exam): 32 questions
- 2.0 Technical Accounting and Reporting (44% of exam): 44 questions
- 3.0 State and Local Governments (24% of exam): 24 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: An analyst computes an entity's current ratio of 1.8x and quick ratio of 0.9x. Which interpretation of these ratios is MOST accurate?**
A: The current ratio indicates adequate overall liquidity, but the quick ratio below 1.0x suggests the entity relies heavily on inventory to meet current obligations, raising a concern about near-term liquidity if inventory cannot be converted quickly

**Q: An entity reports net income of $4,200,000, interest expense of $800,000, income tax expense of $1,200,000, depreciation of $900,000, and amortization of $300,000. Calculate EBITDA.**
A: $7,400,000, EBITDA adds back interest expense, income tax expense, depreciation, and amortization to net income

**Q: Under ASC 350, which event or circumstance is MOST likely to be an indicator that a reporting unit's goodwill may be impaired, triggering a quantitative goodwill impairment test?**
A: A significant adverse change in the business climate such as a substantial loss of key customers representing 30% of the reporting unit's revenue, or a regulatory action that restricts a major product line

**Q: A company is developing internal-use software. During the current period, costs were incurred for: (A) evaluating alternative software vendors; (B) writing application code and unit testing; (C) training end users on the new system. How should each cost be classified under ASC 350-40?**
A: Cost A: expense (preliminary project stage); Cost B: capitalize (application development stage); Cost C: expense (post-implementation/operation stage)

**Q: Under GASB Statement No. 34, what is the measurement focus and basis of accounting used in government-wide financial statements?**
A: Full accrual basis with an economic resources measurement focus, recognizing all assets, deferred outflows, liabilities, and deferred inflows regardless of when cash flows occur

**Q: Which type of governmental fund is used to account for the accumulation of resources for, and the payment of, long-term debt principal and interest?**
A: Debt service fund, accounts for the accumulation of resources for and the payment of general long-term debt principal and interest

## CPA Information Systems and Controls (ISC) (ISC)
Vendor: AICPA
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/cpa-isc/
Total questions: 300

The Information Systems and Controls (ISC) section is one of three Discipline sections of the Uniform CPA Examination administered by the AICPA. Candidates pass three Core sections (AUD, FAR, REG) plus one Discipline of their choice, ISC is most often selected by candidates planning a career in IT audit, cybersecurity, or System and Organization Controls (SOC) attestation. The 4-hour exam consists of 82 multiple-choice questions and 6 task-based simulations, weighted 60% MCQ / 40% TBS in scoring (the only section without 50/50 split). Content covers three areas: Information Systems and Data Management (35-45%): IT infrastructure components, cloud computing models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), enterprise and accounting information systems, system availability, business continuity and disaster recovery, IT change management, data management, relational databases, SQL queries, data warehouses and lakes, and business process modeling; Security, Confidentiality and Privacy (35-45%): HIPAA Security and Privacy Rules, GDPR Articles 4-34, PCI DSS, NIST CSF and Privacy Framework, NIST SP 800-53, CIS Controls v8.1, COBIT 2019, threat types and cyber-attack stages, identification/authentication/authorization controls, encryption, Data Loss Prevention, security testing, and incident response; and Considerations for SOC Engagements (15-25%): purpose and intended users of SOC 1®, SOC 2®, SOC 3®, and SOC for Cybersecurity reports, Trust Services Criteria, system description criteria, complementary user entity controls (CUECs) and complementary subservice organization controls (CSOCs), report opinions and modifications. References include the AICPA Trust Services Criteria, NIST frameworks, HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164, GDPR, PCI DSS, COSO ERM, and COBIT 2019.

### Domains
- 1.0 Information Systems and Data Management (37% of exam): 112 questions
- 2.0 Security, Confidentiality and Privacy (37% of exam): 112 questions
- 3.0 Considerations for System and Organization Controls (SOC) Engagements (26% of exam): 76 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: Which of the following BEST describes the role of network infrastructure within an organization's IT architecture?**
A: Network infrastructure encompasses the hardware and software components, including routers, switches, firewalls, and cabling, that enable communication and data transfer between devices and systems within the organization

**Q: A company contracts with a cloud vendor to use the vendor's servers, storage, and networking equipment, but the company installs and manages its own operating systems, middleware, and applications. Which cloud computing service model does this arrangement BEST describe?**
A: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), because the vendor provides the underlying hardware infrastructure while the company manages the software stack above it

**Q: Under HIPAA, which entities are classified as 'covered entities' and are directly subject to the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules?**
A: Health plans, health care clearinghouses, and health care providers that transmit health information electronically, these three categories directly handle protected health information as part of their core functions

**Q: The GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) establishes six principles relating to the processing of personal data. Which principle requires that personal data be collected only for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes?**
A: Purpose limitation, personal data shall be collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a way incompatible with those purposes

**Q: The AICPA Trust Services Criteria (TSC) are organized into five categories. Which option correctly lists all five Trust Services categories?**
A: Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, Privacy

**Q: A payroll processing service organization's clients are public companies subject to Sarbanes-Oxley. The clients' external auditors need assurance about the payroll processor's controls relevant to the clients' internal control over financial reporting. Which SOC report BEST meets this need?**
A: SOC 1, a report specifically designed to address controls at a service organization that are relevant to user entities' internal control over financial reporting (ICFR), used by user entities and their auditors for financial statement audit purposes

## CPA Tax Compliance and Planning (TCP) (TCP)
Vendor: AICPA
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/cpa-tcp/
Total questions: 124

The Tax Compliance and Planning (TCP) section is one of three Discipline sections of the Uniform CPA Examination administered by the AICPA. Candidates pass three Core sections (AUD, FAR, REG) plus one Discipline of their choice, TCP is most often selected by candidates planning a career in tax compliance, tax advisory, or personal financial planning. The 4-hour exam consists of 68 multiple-choice questions and 7 task-based simulations, weighted 50/50 in scoring. Content covers four areas: Tax Compliance and Planning for Individuals and Personal Financial Planning (30-40%), incentive compensation, AMT, at-risk and passive activity loss limitations, gifting and unified transfer tax, retirement plan selection (IRA, Roth, 401(k), annuities), investment risk, education funding, life and long-term care insurance, beneficiary designations, return on investment net of tax; Entity Tax Compliance (30-40%): C corporation NOL and capital loss carryforwards, shareholder contributions and distributions, consolidated 1120 returns, international tax (CFC, FDII, BEAT, GILTI, IC-DISC, permanent establishment), S corporation shareholder basis and AAA, partnership partner basis and elections, trusts (simple, complex, grantor), distributable net income, tax-exempt organizations and unrelated business income; Entity Tax Planning (10-20%): entity selection and formation, tax planning for C corps, S corps, and partnerships, built-in gains tax, terminating S elections; and Property Transactions (10-20%): like-kind exchanges, involuntary conversions, Section 1231 capital gains and ordinary losses, Section 1245 and 1250 depreciation recapture, unrecaptured Section 1250 gain, Section 1244 small business stock, installment sales, related-party transactions, imputed interest. References include the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 as amended, Treasury Regulations, and case law on federal taxation.

### Domains
- 1.0 Tax Compliance and Planning for Individuals and Personal Financial Planning (32% of exam): 40 questions
- 2.0 Entity Tax Compliance (42% of exam): 52 questions
- 3.0 Entity Tax Planning (16% of exam): 20 questions
- 4.0 Property Transactions (Disposition of Assets) (10% of exam): 12 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: An employee exercises an incentive stock option (ISO) and purchases 1,000 shares of employer stock at the option price of $10 per share when the fair market value is $35 per share. The employee holds all shares and does not sell them during the current year. What is the tax consequence for regular federal income tax purposes in the year of exercise?**
A: No regular income tax consequence occurs in the year of exercise, ISOs are not taxable for regular tax purposes when exercised if no same-year sale occurs

**Q: The Kiddie Tax rules under IRC §1(g) tax a child's net unearned income at the parent's marginal tax rate. Which taxpayer situation is MOST likely subject to the Kiddie Tax?**
A: A 17-year-old who has $4,800 of dividend income and $500 of earned income from babysitting, and can be claimed as a dependent by her parents

**Q: Under current federal tax law applicable to C corporations, what are the carryover rules for a net operating loss (NOL) generated in a tax year beginning after December 31, 2017?**
A: NOLs may only be carried forward indefinitely, with the deduction in any carryover year limited to 80% of the corporation's taxable income (computed before the NOL deduction) for that year

**Q: Under IRC §351, a taxpayer contributes property with a fair market value of $90,000 and an adjusted basis of $30,000 to a newly formed corporation in exchange for 100% of the stock. No other consideration is received. What is the tax treatment for the contributing taxpayer?**
A: The taxpayer recognizes no gain or loss; the taxpayer's basis in the stock received equals $30,000 (substituted basis equal to the adjusted basis of the property contributed)

**Q: Three investors are forming a new business and are deciding between organizing as a C corporation, an S corporation, or a partnership. They anticipate losses in the first two years followed by significant profitability. Which characteristic is UNIQUE to S corporations and restricts their use?**
A: S corporations are limited to 100 shareholders, may only issue one class of stock, and cannot have nonresident alien shareholders or most entity shareholders (with limited exceptions)

**Q: A C corporation expects taxable income of $500,000 in the current year and has $300,000 of NOL carryforwards from prior years (all post-2017). The corporation wants to minimize its current-year federal income tax. What is the maximum NOL deduction the corporation may claim?**
A: $400,000, the corporation may deduct 80% of the $500,000 taxable income, which is more than the available $300,000 NOL carryforward, so the full $300,000 is deductible

## Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH) (CEH)
Vendor: EC-Council
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/ceh/
Total questions: 700

Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH) from EC-Council validates offensive security skills for penetration testers, SOC analysts, and security engineers. The current blueprint (v5.0) covers nine domains: Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview (6%), methodologies, frameworks, controls, laws; Reconnaissance Techniques (17%): footprinting, network scanning, enumeration; System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques (15%), vulnerability analysis, system hacking, malware threats; Network and Perimeter Hacking (24%): sniffing, social engineering, denial-of-service, session hijacking, evading IDS/firewalls/honeypots; Web Application Hacking (14%): web servers, web applications, SQL injection; Wireless Network Hacking (5%); Mobile Platform, IoT, and OT Hacking (10%); Cloud Computing (5%): container, serverless, cloud security; and Cryptography (5%). CEH is ANSI/ISO 17024 accredited and DoD 8570/8140 baseline approved for several cybersecurity roles. Often compared with OSCP (more hands-on offensive) and CompTIA PenTest+ (vendor-neutral).

### Domains
- 1.0 Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview (4% of exam): 28 questions
- 2.0 Reconnaissance Techniques (18% of exam): 128 questions
- 3.0 System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques (14% of exam): 100 questions
- 4.0 Network and Perimeter Hacking (22% of exam): 156 questions
- 5.0 Web Application Hacking (19% of exam): 128 questions
- 6.0 Wireless Network Hacking (5% of exam): 36 questions
- 7.0 Mobile Platform, IoT, and OT Hacking (9% of exam): 60 questions
- 8.0 Cloud Computing (4% of exam): 28 questions
- 9.0 Cryptography (5% of exam): 36 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: Which three properties form the CIA triad that serves as the foundational framework for all information security programs?**
A: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability

**Q: What is the PRIMARY distinction between passive and active reconnaissance in the context of ethical hacking?**
A: Passive reconnaissance gathers intelligence without directly interacting with the target system; active reconnaissance directly probes or interacts with the target, risking detection

**Q: Which type of vulnerability assessment tests a system from the perspective of an unauthenticated external attacker with no prior knowledge of or credentials for the target environment?**
A: External black-box assessment, simulates an outside attacker with no credentials or internal knowledge

**Q: How does a MAC flooding attack work against a network switch, and what is the result when the CAM table is exhausted?**
A: MAC flooding sends frames with thousands of unique fake source MAC addresses, exhausting the switch's Content Addressable Memory (CAM) table, when full, many switches fail open and flood all frames out all ports (behaving like a hub), enabling passive sniffing

**Q: Which web server component handles incoming HTTP requests, routes them to the appropriate application logic, and returns the resulting HTTP responses to clients?**
A: Web server software (Apache, nginx, IIS), the HTTP server process that receives connections, parses requests, and delivers responses

**Q: In wireless networking, what does the term SSID (Service Set Identifier) refer to?**
A: The human-readable name that identifies a wireless network, broadcast in AP beacon frames

## CompTIA Project+ (PK0-005)
Vendor: CompTIA
URL: https://quizbuffet.com/comptia-project-plus/
Total questions: 812

CompTIA Project+ certifies the ability to manage the project life cycle, coordinate small-to-medium-sized projects, build a communication plan, manage resources and stakeholders, maintain project documentation and artifacts, and support larger IT projects. The exam covers both waterfall and agile methodologies and measures knowledge equivalent to 6-12 months of hands-on IT project management experience.

### Domains
- Project Management Concepts (38% of exam): 308 questions
- Project Life Cycle Phases (31% of exam): 252 questions
- Tools and Documentation (10% of exam): 84 questions
- Basics of IT and Governance (21% of exam): 168 questions

### Sample questions
**Q: How hard is the CompTIA Project+ exam?**
A: It is one of the more approachable project management exams. It tests practical knowledge of the project life cycle, communication, and basic agile and waterfall concepts rather than deep formulas. With focused study, most people pass without prior certification.

**Q: How many questions are on the Project+ exam?**
A: You get a maximum of 90 multiple-choice and performance-based questions in 90 minutes. QuizBuffet covers every exam domain so you know what to expect going in.

**Q: What score do you need to pass Project+?**
A: You need 710 on a scale of 100 to 900. It is pass or fail, so aim for steady coverage across all the domains rather than mastering one area.

**Q: Does CompTIA Project+ expire?**
A: No. Unlike Security+, Project+ does not expire and is valid for life once you earn it, so there are no renewal fees or continuing education requirements.

**Q: Do you need experience before taking Project+?**
A: It is not required, but CompTIA recommends about 6 to 12 months of hands-on experience coordinating or managing small projects. Beginners pass regularly by pairing study with practice questions.

**Q: Is CompTIA Project+ worth it?**
A: Yes, if you are moving into project coordination or IT project management. It proves core project skills without the experience hours that bigger credentials demand, which makes it a strong first step.
